clue.text: Able to restore compliance at first in central banks

indicators.note: banks line the sides of a river, so the word for central encloses the other letters

parts.note: medial means situated in the middle

indicators.note: only the opening letter of compliance is wanted

explanation.surface: Talk of reviving obedience among the central banks of the financial world.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Central banks' looks like a financial term; here 'central' gives MEDIAL and 'banks' tells you it holds C (first letter of 'compliance') plus IN.
explanation.definitionFit: A remedy with healing properties is one able to restore health.

clue.text: Frenchman excited in ungodly place

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for Monsieur, a Frenchman
agog means eagerly excited

explanation.surface: A worked-up Frenchman finds himself somewhere wicked.
explanation.walkthrough: Magog is the land of the enemies of God in the Bible, paired with Gog, hence an ungodly place.
explanation.definitionFit: In Ezekiel and Revelation the biblical land opposed to God's people bears this name.

clue.text: Climbing, setter's cutting palm tree branch off

indicators.note: the setter's letters slice into the tree, sitting inside it

parts.note: a date is a kind of palm tree

indicators.note: in a down clue climbing means the letters read upwards, backwards

parts.note: the setter would say I've, I have

explanation.surface: Someone climbing a palm tree saws a branch off it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Branch off' looks like the setter's pruning, but it is the definition, a verb meaning to diverge; 'Climbing' signals reading upwards in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To deviate is to diverge or turn aside from a path, as a road branches off.

clue.text: Caught group in army base

indicators.note: something caught is heard, so the army word is taken as spoken

parts.note: a corps is a body of troops within an army

explanation.surface: A unit is captured at an army base.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Caught' looks like the cricket C, but here it means heard: CORPS is said like CORE.
explanation.definitionFit: The core of something is its essential basis or central foundation.

clue.text: Slowcoach shaking off top cop

indicators.note: the first letter of the slow creature is removed in a down clue

parts.note: a snail is the proverbial slowcoach

explanation.surface: A sluggish policeman gets rid of a senior officer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cop' is the verb here, to catch or arrest, not a police officer.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal verbs for catching or arresting a wrongdoer.

clue.text: Feller tricked about European turtle

parts.note: a logger fells trees

indicators.note: the deceived word goes round the European abbreviation

parts.note: had means fooled, as in 'you've been had'

explanation.surface: A man was duped by some European turtle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Feller' is a tree-cutter, not a man.
explanation.definitionFit: The loggerhead is a large-headed sea turtle species.

clue.text: House fixed in advance

definitions.meaning: to accommodate someone, give them lodging
rigged beforehand, as in a rigged job

explanation.surface: A house that was arranged beforehand.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means to lodge a guest; the hyphenated adjective means secretly prearranged.

clue.text: Diviner Wessex girl mounted by forward man

indicators.note: in a down clue the girl sits beneath the other letters

parts.note: a prop is a forward in rugby
he is a man
Tess of the d'Urbervilles, Hardy's heroine of his fictional Wessex

explanation.surface: A Wessex girl with second sight is ridden by a forward man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Forward' is a rugby position, PROP, not a bold attitude.
explanation.definitionFit: A female seer foretells the future, as a diviner does.

clue.text: Cryptic hint on vent into which one disappears

indicators.note: cryptic means obscured, so the letters of hint are jumbled

parts.note: to air a view is to vent it

explanation.surface: A puzzling clue about a vent through which someone escapes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cryptic' rearranges HINT to THIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: people vanish into thin air, leaving no trace.

clue.text: Boris: leader of party, awful sneak and rat

indicators.note: only the first letter of party is used
awful suggests a mess, so the letters of sneak and rat are rearranged

explanation.surface: Boris, the head of a party, is a dreadful sneak and rat.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface points at Boris Johnson; the Boris meant is the Russian author of Doctor Zhivago. 'Awful' rearranges SNEAK and RAT to ASTERNAK.
explanation.definitionFit: Boris Pasternak was the Russian novelist and poet who wrote Doctor Zhivago.

clue.text: Leading Brexiteer Boris ending, unfortunately, ruling people

parts.note: Michael Gove was a prominent campaigner for Brexit

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things gone wrong, so those letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A top Leave campaigner regrets the end of Boris's reign.
explanation.walkthrough: Michael Gove is a British Conservative politician. 'Unfortunately' rearranges BORIS ENDING to RNINGBODIES.
explanation.definitionFit: Councils and boards that govern organisations are people who rule.

clue.text: Bet everything Spain makes a mark in football

parts.note: in poker, to go all in is to stake all one's chips
E is the international vehicle code for Spain

explanation.surface: Wager the lot on Spain scoring in a football match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mark' is a line marked on the pitch, not a score.
explanation.definitionFit: The painted line between the posts on a pitch is a marking that the ball must cross to score.

clue.text: Amend E sharp bum note covers

indicators.note: the musical note wraps round the other letters

parts.note: re is the second note of the sol-fa scale

indicators.note: bum means bad or wrong, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A musician corrects a wrong E sharp that keeps being covered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bum' is British slang for bad or useless, here the signal to rearrange; 'covers' means the musical note encloses the result.
explanation.definitionFit: To reword something is to amend or alter its wording.

clue.text: Ali G follows foreign character, one foolish target

indicators.note: the letter G comes after the Greek letter

parts.note: Muhammad Ali was born Cassius Clay
pi is a letter of the Greek alphabet

indicators.note: foolish suggests disorder, so the letters of one are scrambled

explanation.surface: Ali G, the comic, comes after some foreign oddball, a silly target.
explanation.walkthrough: Ali G is a British comedy character; here 'Ali' is the boxer, born Cassius CLAY. 'Foolish' rearranges ONE to EON.
explanation.definitionFit: A clay disc flung into the air is the target in trap shooting.

clue.text: His sentences add up to life

definitions.text: His sentences add up to life

parts.words: His sentences add up to life
parts.note: a writer whose sentences together tell someone's life story; also a judge's punishments that total a life term

explanation.surface: A harsh judge whose penalties amount to life imprisonment.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a judge passing sentences; the sentences are written ones that together tell a person's life.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who writes life stories assembles sentences into an account of a life.

clue.text: Drunkenly outspoken, narcissistic creature in the main

indicators.note: spoken with a drunk's slur, so the word is said as it would come out

parts.note: self-obsessed, putting oneself first

explanation.surface: A tipsy, loud, self-absorbed person.
explanation.walkthrough: Slurred, SELFISH comes out as SHELFISH. 'The main' is an old word for the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Crabs, lobsters and oysters are creatures of the sea, which poets call the main.

clue.text: Careless friends lifted very soft grass skirts

indicators.note: in a down clue lifted means the letters read upward, backwards

parts.note: pals are friends

indicators.note: the grass word goes around the musical letters

parts.note: hay is dried grass
pp, pianissimo, is very soft in music

explanation.surface: Careless friends hoisted some very soft grass skirts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grass skirts' reads as hula costume, but 'skirts' is a verb: the grass goes round the very-soft musical marking. 'Lifted' reads upward in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Slap-happy means casual and haphazard, so it is a synonym of careless.

clue.text: Retire, having left new regional capital

indicators.note: the letter for new has departed

parts.note: to turn in is to go to bed

explanation.surface: Someone retires, leaving for a new regional capital.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove one N from TURN IN.
explanation.definitionFit: This Italian city is the capital of the Piedmont region.

clue.text: Use a description of cider?

definitions.meaning: to put something to use, employ it
cider tastes of apples, so it is apple-y

explanation.surface: Is this a word for describing cider?
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading takes the word as apple-y, tasting of apples.
explanation.definitionFit: To employ a method is to put it to use; cider, made from apples, could be called apple-y.

clue.text: Greek First Lady's assistant straddling two gates

indicators.note: the assistant's letters stand on either side of the gates

parts.note: PA is a personal assistant
AND and OR are logic gates in electronics

explanation.surface: A Greek president's wife has an aide who stands astride two gates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gates' are logic gates, AND and OR, not garden gates.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth she was the first woman, made by the gods, who opened the jar of evils.

clue.text: Transparent ornaments, say, in some minimalist American music?

definitions.text: say, in some minimalist American music?
definitions.meaning: a piece by Philip Glass, the American minimalist composer

explanation.surface: Are see-through decorations a kind of American minimalism?
explanation.walkthrough: Philip Glass is the American minimalist composer, so a piece of his is a Glass work.
explanation.definitionFit: Glass objects made as decoration; and a composition by Philip Glass.

clue.text: Poet cut capers in the tube

parts.note: Ovid was the Roman poet of the Metamorphoses

indicators.note: to caper is to frolic about, so the letters of cut are jumbled

explanation.surface: A poet larks about on the London Underground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capers' looks like a noun but it is the anagram signal on CUT. 'The tube' suggests London's Underground, but it is the body's tube.
explanation.definitionFit: The passage carrying eggs from the ovary is an anatomical tube.

clue.text: Maybe scratch both sides of Hindustani hat

parts.note: the two outer letters of Hindustani are H and I, spelt out with and between them
a cap is a hat

explanation.surface: Perhaps scratch the edges of an Indian hat.
explanation.walkthrough: In golf a scratch player has a handicap of zero, so scratch is one example of a handicap.
explanation.definitionFit: In golf, scratch is the zero rating given to an expert player, one example of this allowance.

clue.text: See 10
Turned around in cockney's area of London

indicators.note: a cockney drops the H at the start of words

parts.note: Hendon is a district of north London

explanation.surface: A cockney came back round to their part of London.
explanation.walkthrough: HENDON is in north London; cockneys drop their h's, so it becomes 'ENDON.
explanation.definitionFit: Something turned so its end faces you is positioned with its tip foremost.

clue.text: Stick around American island

indicators.note: the sticky word goes round the letter for American

parts.note: gum sticks things together

explanation.surface: Stay close to an American island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stick' is the noun or verb for glue, not staying put.
explanation.definitionFit: This western Pacific territory of the USA is an island.

clue.text: About to welcome group flying in port

indicators.note: the word for about takes the airline letters inside it

parts.note: on means about, concerning
BA is British Airways, a company that flies

explanation.surface: About to greet a group of people flying in to a harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About to' looks like 'on the point of', but 'About' is its own piece and 'to welcome' is the container signal. Oban is a port on Scotland's west coast.
explanation.definitionFit: This west Highland town is a harbour serving the Hebridean ferries.

clue.text: For yours truly, where Trump is certain to create tragedy

parts.note: pro means in favour of
the setter referring to themself, me
Donald Trump was in the US as president
bound means certain, as in bound to happen

explanation.surface: Speaking for myself, Trump's homeland is sure to stage a tragedy.
explanation.walkthrough: PRO ME THE US BOUND.
explanation.definitionFit: This Greek drama attributed to Aeschylus is a tragedy about the Titan chained to a rock.

clue.text: Desire what's finally in butterfly net

indicators.note: the last letter of the insect's name is used

parts.note: to net money is to earn it

explanation.surface: A collector wants what ends up in the butterfly net.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Net' is the verb, to clear a profit.
explanation.definitionFit: To yearn is to long for something, a synonym of desire as a verb.

clue.text: Spy once noting criminal on edge

indicators.note: the scrambled letters sit beside the word for edge

parts.note: a rim is an edge

indicators.note: criminal suggests wrongdoing, so the letters are shuffled

explanation.surface: A former spy notes a crook on the brink.
explanation.walkthrough: Stella Rimington was head of MI5, Britain's security service. 'Criminal' rearranges NOTING to INGTON.
explanation.definitionFit: Dame Stella Rimington headed MI5 in the 1990s, so she was once a spymaster.
